question: hi im a first year and dont know anyone yet, who should i contact if i want to find clubs or ways to meet people on campus?

body.answer:
That sounds really hard, and a lot of students feel this way, especially at first. You're not the only one.

A great way to meet people is to explore the more than 100 clubs and organizations, which include cultural, academic, religious, recreational, entertainment, political, social, and special-interest groups. All clubs are open to all students and welcome new members. Browse the club listing: [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) [25]

You can start exploring on Archway ([http://archway.ramapo.edu/](http://archway.ramapo.edu/)) or download the Archway App from the [Apple Store](https://archway.ramapo.edu/click?linkid=08fd1643-7962-4f57-b38c-3f5860d0d5dd) or [Google Play](https://archway.ramapo.edu/click?linkid=919b2f1c-98bd-4bbf-866a-034302ac992d). [14]

For help getting involved or finding community, contact the Center for Student Involvement or the Office of Access, Belonging and Community. [23][34]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [55]

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [56]

Sources: [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/commuter-affairs/involvement-frequently-asked-questions/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/oabc/home/you-belong-at-ramapo/) [55](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [56](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
That sounds really hard, and a lot of students feel this way, especially at first. You're not the only one.

A great way to meet people is to explore the more than 100 clubs and organizations, which include cultural, academic, religious, recreational, entertainment, political, social, and special-interest groups. All clubs are open to all students and welcome new members. Browse the club listing: [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) [25]

You can start exploring on Archway ([http://archway.ramapo.edu/](http://archway.ramapo.edu/)) or download the Archway App from the [Apple Store](https://archway.ramapo.edu/click?linkid=08fd1643-7962-4f57-b38c-3f5860d0d5dd) or [Google Play](https://archway.ramapo.edu/click?linkid=919b2f1c-98bd-4bbf-866a-034302ac992d). [14]

For help getting involved or finding community, contact the Center for Student Involvement or the Office of Access, Belonging and Community. [23][34]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [55]

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [56]

Sources: [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/commuter-affairs/involvement-frequently-asked-questions/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/oabc/home/you-belong-at-ramapo/) [55](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [56](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I'm a sophomore business major and need to talk to someone about switching to accounting. Who is the director or chair I should email and where is their office?

body.answer:
The college catalog names the program convener of Accounting (Accounting BS, Accounting MS, Accounting 4+1, Accounting Minor) [16][17][18][19]:
- Constance Crawford, program convener, Professor of Accounting, ccrawfor@ramapo.edu, office ASB-304 [20]

The directory lists no chair, head, convener, director or dean for accounting, and no chair, head, convener, director or dean for business. The dean of the Anisfield School of Business is Ed Petkus (Dean) [2]. The catalog names Constance Crawford as Accounting’s program convener; her office is ASB-304 [16][17][18][19][20]. To ask about switching majors, contact the Anisfield School of Business at asb@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7379 [10].

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [21]

question: who is the best professor for intro to biology? i heard some are way easier

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Faculty profiles that list BIOL 101 Introduction to Biology among the courses they teach:
- Paramjeet Bagga, Professor of Biology, pbagga@ramapo.edu [15]
- Yan Xu, Professor of Biology, yxu@ramapo.edu [16]
A profile lists the courses a professor teaches; it doesn't say who teaches which section this term.

The profiles identify faculty who teach BIOL 101, but they do not rate professors or say who is easier. [15] [16] I don't have verified information about who can help you decide which professor to choose. The School of Science, Nursing, and Health Office is the most likely office to ask.

Sources: [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/snh/faculty/paramjeet-bagga/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/snh/faculty/yan-xu/)

question: Who is the director of the Center for Health and Counseling Services? Also what's the phone number

body.answer:
**Health Services**

Name: Health Services [Source](https://www.valleyhealth.com/save-your-spot-ramapo-college-health-services)

Phones: (201) 684-7536 [Source](https://www.valleyhealth.com/save-your-spot-ramapo-college-health-services)

Contact note: Appointments can be made by calling 201-684-7536 or through VMG’s Save Your Spot service. Drop-in visits are always welcome. Medicat Patient Portal: immunize@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.valleyhealth.com/save-your-spot-ramapo-college-health-services)

Related Resources: Student Health Insurance \([https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/student-health-insurance/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/student-health-insurance/)\) Center for Student Wellness \([https://www.ramapo.edu/chcs/](https://www.ramapo.edu/chcs/)\) Counseling Services \([https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/)\) Substance Use Disorder \(SUD\) \([https://www.ramapo.edu/sud/](https://www.ramapo.edu/sud/)\) Sexual Harassment Resources \([https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-harassment-resources/](https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-harassment-resources/)\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/health/)

Health Services: Ramapo College has partnered with Valley Medical Group to manage our on-campus Health Services Center. This agreement ensures that students and employees have direct access to high-quality clinical care, virtual telehealth visits, and coordinated referrals to Valley specialists throughout northern New Jersey. View Valley Medical Group Health Services \([https://www.valleyhealth.com/ramapo-college-he…](https://www.valleyhealth.com/ramapo-college-he…) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/health/)

**Counseling Center**

Name: Counseling Center [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/)

Phones: (201) 684-7522 [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/)

Contact note: To learn more about our services or to schedule an appointment, please visit us in the Academic Building D, Room 216, or call our office at \(201\) 684-7522. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/)

About the Staff: Judith Green, Psy.D., Director, Center for Student Wellness \([https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/judith-green/](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/judith-green/)\) Michael A. Pino, DSW, LCSW, LCADC, Associate Director, Counseling Services \([https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/Michael-a.-pino](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/Michael-a.-pino)\) Debra Verret, LCSW, LCADC, Psychological Counselor \([https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/deb/](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/deb/)\) Elena Yee, LPC, Psychological Counselor \([https://www.ramapo.edu/counsel…](https://www.ramapo.edu/counsel…) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/about-the-staff/)

Senior Supervising Staff: The following are doctoral level psychologists who supervise psychology intern trainees: Judith Green, Psy.D., Director, Center for Student Wellness Michael A. Pino, DSW, LCSW, LCADC, Associate Director for Counseling Services [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/training-programs/)

Relevant Experience: Dr. Green is a New Jersey licensed psychologist with more than 25 years of experience working in university and college counseling centers. She completed her pre-doctoral internship at SUNY-Albany’s Counseling Center. She worked in the counseling centers at Seton Hall University and William Paterson University prior to becoming the Director of the Center for Health and Counseling Services at Ramap… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/judith-green/)

Connect With Us: To learn more about our services or to schedule an appointment, please visit us in the Academic Building D, Room 216, or call our office at \(201\) 684-7522. Academic Year Hours: Monday – Friday: 8:30 am – 4:30 pm Summer Hours: Monday – Thursday: 8:00 am – 5:15 pm Closed on Fridays [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/)

**Dean of Students**

Update to Health Services: From: The Dean of Students <deanofstudents@ramapo.edu> Date: Fri, Feb 27, 2026 Subject: Update to Health Services Dear Students: As of Monday, March 2, 2026 and through Tuesday, May 12, 2026, Ramapo College will offer free, telehealth services to all students via Bergen New Bridge Medical Center. Appointments will be available Monday through Sunday \(7 days per week\) from 10:00am to 6:00pm. Many me… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/student-communications/update-to-health-services-feb2026/)

Supporting the Well-Being of Students: The Center for Student Wellness is a multi-disciplinary team which offers free, confidential mental health counseling, crisis intervention, and health promotion services. The unit is staffed by psychologists, social workers, and professional counselors with bilingual staff who speak Spanish. Counseling Services also has a collaborating psychiatrist and Alcohol and Other Drug Counselors. The contac… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/student-communications/mental-health-and-well-being-resources-fall-2026/)

question: Is there a Latino or Hispanic cultural club at Ramapo, and how do I get in touch with them?

body.answer:
Yes. Ramapo lists several Latino/Hispanic-related groups, including the Association of Latinos Moving Ahead (ALMA), Organization of Latino Unity (OLU), and Association of Latino Professionals for America (ALPFA). [2][3][5][11][12][13]

You can contact ALMA at alma08@ramapo.edu, OLU at olu@ramapo.edu, or ALPFA at alpfa@ramapo.edu. [3][5][11] The Spanish Club is also an option for people passionate about Spanish language and culture; email spanishclub@ramapo.edu. [4][9]

Their listings are available at [ALMA](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/association-latinos-moving-ahead/), [OLU](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/organization-of-latino-unity-olu/), [ALPFA](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/association-of-latino-professionals-for-america-alpfa/), and [Spanish Club](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/spanish-club/). For help connecting with cultural organizations, contact the Multicultural Center and the Office of Access, Belonging and Community.

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [64]

Yes—there are several gaming-related clubs. Ramapo Esports is open to all students to learn about and offers open events; tryouts are required for exclusive membership as an RCNJ Esports Player [18]. Ramapo Gamers Club welcomes casual and competitive players and holds meetings about esports events [19].

For tabletop/board games, Geek and Nerd Culture has D&D campaigns and board game nights [15,24]. Trading Card Game Club welcomes new, casual, and competitive players [20,25]. Other options include Ramapo Girls in Gaming [17,23], Ramapo Smash Club [16,26], and Rhythm Game Club, which holds weekly meetings and casual tournaments [22].

question: how do i join a club? i'm a sophomore and haven't joined anything yet

body.answer:
Browse the club list at [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) or explore Archway at [http://archway.ramapo.edu/](http://archway.ramapo.edu/); you can also download the Archway App in the Apple Store or Google Play. Clubs cover cultural, academic, religious, recreational, entertainment, political, social and special interests. All clubs listed are open to all students, welcome new members, ideas and directions, and are run by students under the general supervision of the Center for Student Involvement. [4][9]

As a sophomore, you might check out Sophomores Advancing In Leadership (S.A.I.L): [https://archway.ramapo.edu/SAIL/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/SAIL/). [1] Math Club, History Club, Spanish Club, or other listed groups may also interest you; for example, Math Club welcomes students who enjoy problem-solving and mathematics, while History Club is open to all majors. [33][38]

If your interests aren’t represented, inquire at the Center for Student Involvement about starting a new club or organization. [9]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [54]
- **Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [54]

question: is there a pre-med or pre-law club

question: when does the student government association meet and can regular students go to the meetings?

body.answer:
Senate meetings are Mondays at 7 p.m. in ASB 230. General meetings are Wednesdays at 1 p.m.; locations vary. The listed upcoming general meeting is 11/18 at Friends Hall. [3]

Yes. Senate and General Meetings are open to the public, and anyone interested in addressing SGA may speak during “Public Comment.” [3]

**Student Government Association**: Phone: (201) 684-7271. Email: sga@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-225. [32]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/sga/meetings/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: which club is the best one to join for making friends? i dont know anyone

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes. That sounds really hard, and a lot of students feel this way, especially at first. You're not the only one.

There isn’t one published “best” club for making friends. Ramapo says joining clubs can provide “interesting friends”; all listed clubs are open to all students, and welcome new members, ideas and directions. Each group operates under its own constitution, according to its members’ interests and enthusiasm. [8]

For a group explicitly focused on bringing people together, the Culture Club’s mission is “to bring people together by sharing each other's culture.” [30] Math Club describes itself as a community and says it is an opportunity to “meet and connect with others.” [39] The Association of Latinos Moving Ahead’s page invites students who want to “make a great group of friends,” and says everyone is welcome. [12]

Browse the club list at [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) or explore Archway and its app. [2] The Center for Student Involvement supervises clubs and is the office to ask about choosing a club or starting one. [8]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [54]

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [55]

answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes. That sounds really hard, and a lot of students feel this way, especially at first. You're not the only one.

There isn’t one published “best” club for making friends. Ramapo says joining clubs can provide “interesting friends”; all listed clubs are open to all students, and welcome new members, ideas and directions. Each group operates under its own constitution, according to its members’ interests and enthusiasm. [8]

For a group explicitly focused on bringing people together, the Culture Club’s mission is “to bring people together by sharing each other's culture.” [30] Math Club describes itself as a community and says it is an opportunity to “meet and connect with others.” [39] The Association of Latinos Moving Ahead’s page invites students who want to “make a great group of friends,” and says everyone is welcome. [12]

Browse the club list at [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) or explore Archway and its app. [2] The Center for Student Involvement supervises clubs and is the office to ask about choosing a club or starting one. [8]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [54]

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [55]

question: what is CMPS 147 about and how many credits is it

body.answer:
CMPS 147, COMPUTER SCIENCE I, is a 4-credit course. It introduces computer-based problem-solving and basic computer systems, the ANSI C++ programming language, algorithm design, program development, debugging, testing and documentation. Topics include variables, data types, expressions, selection, repetition, functions and arrays. A course fee is required. It carries the Gen Ed 18-Quantitative Rsng (GEQR) attribute. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CMPS147)

answer:
CMPS 147, COMPUTER SCIENCE I, is a 4-credit course. It introduces computer-based problem-solving and basic computer systems, the ANSI C++ programming language, algorithm design, program development, debugging, testing and documentation. Topics include variables, data types, expressions, selection, repetition, functions and arrays. A course fee is required. It carries the Gen Ed 18-Quantitative Rsng (GEQR) attribute. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CMPS147)

question: Do I need to take PSYC 101 before I can take abnormal psychology or can I take them at the same time?

body.answer:
PSYC 101 is not a published prerequisite for PSYC 314. PSYC 314 lists only CRWT 102 CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II or CRWT 102S CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II as its prerequisite. [2][3] The catalog does not say whether you can take them at the same time. The Registrar says to review prerequisites in Web Self Service and that it is your responsibility to complete all prerequisites before registering. [11]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [15]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PSYC101) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PSYC314) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
PSYC 101 is not a published prerequisite for PSYC 314. PSYC 314 lists only CRWT 102 CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II or CRWT 102S CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II as its prerequisite. [2][3] The catalog does not say whether you can take them at the same time. The Registrar says to review prerequisites in Web Self Service and that it is your responsibility to complete all prerequisites before registering. [11]

The Computer Science BS (Bachelor of Science) requires these courses [1]:

Required courses: CMPS 147 Computer Science I; CMPS 148 Computer Science II; CMPS 220 Assembly Language Programming; CMPS 231 Data Structures; CMPS 311 Operating Systems; CMPS 361 Software Design; CMPS 366 Organization of Programming Languages; CMPS 450 Senior Project; MATH 121 Calculus I; and MATH 205 Mathematical Structures or MATH 237 Discrete Structures. Math electives: choose 2 courses from MATH 122 Calculus II; MATH 124; MATH 200 Independent Study: Mathematics; MATH 225 Multivariable Calculus; MATH 240 Cryptography; MATH 245 Numerical Analysis; MATH 253 Probability; MATH 262 Linear Algebra; MATH 282 Number Theory; MATH 290 Topics; MATH 300 Independent Study: Mathematics; MATH 305 Differential Equations; MATH 321 Geometry; MATH 339 Complex Variables; MATH 353 Statistics or MATH 370 Applied Statistics; MATH 360 Stochastic Calculus for Finance; MATH 390 Advanced Topics. [1]

Computer science electives: choose 7 courses from CMPS 240 Data Analytics in Python or CMPS 285 Mobile Development; CMPS 305 Cyber Security; CMPS 310 Big Data Programming; CMPS 315 The Linux Environment; CMPS 320 Machine Learning; CMPS 327 Network Programming; CMPS 331 Artificial Intelligence; CMPS 335 Agent Engineering; CMPS 337 Computer Vision; CMPS 342 Computer Graphics; CMPS 345 Analysis of Algorithms; CMPS 350 Financial Modeling; CMPS 357 The .NET Environment; CMPS 364 Database Design; CMPS 367 Advanced Topics; CMPS 369 Web Application Development; CMPS 370 Cyber and Network Defense; CMPS 373 Object Oriented Programming; CMPS 375 Mobile Robotics; DATA 301 Data Analysis & Visualization. [1]

Career Pathways courses: PATH 001 Career Pathways Mod 1, PATH 002 Career Pathways Mod 2, and PATH 003 Career Pathways Mod 3. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-CMPS)

answer:
The Computer Science BS (Bachelor of Science) requires these courses [1]:

Required courses: CMPS 147 Computer Science I; CMPS 148 Computer Science II; CMPS 220 Assembly Language Programming; CMPS 231 Data Structures; CMPS 311 Operating Systems; CMPS 361 Software Design; CMPS 366 Organization of Programming Languages; CMPS 450 Senior Project; MATH 121 Calculus I; and MATH 205 Mathematical Structures or MATH 237 Discrete Structures. [1]

Math electives: choose 2 courses from MATH 122 Calculus II; MATH 124; MATH 200 Independent Study: Mathematics; MATH 225 Multivariable Calculus; MATH 240 Cryptography; MATH 245 Numerical Analysis; MATH 253 Probability; MATH 262 Linear Algebra; MATH 282 Number Theory; MATH 290 Topics; MATH 300 Independent Study: Mathematics; MATH 305 Differential Equations; MATH 321 Geometry; MATH 339 Complex Variables; MATH 353 Statistics or MATH 370 Applied Statistics; MATH 360 Stochastic Calculus for Finance; MATH 390 Advanced Topics. [1]

Computer science electives: choose 7 courses from CMPS 240 Data Analytics in Python or CMPS 285 Mobile Development; CMPS 305 Cyber Security; CMPS 310 Big Data Programming; CMPS 315 The Linux Environment; CMPS 320 Machine Learning; CMPS 327 Network Programming; CMPS 331 Artificial Intelligence; CMPS 335 Agent Engineering; CMPS 337 Computer Vision; CMPS 342 Computer Graphics; CMPS 345 Analysis of Algorithms; CMPS 350 Financial Modeling; CMPS 357 The .NET Environment; CMPS 364 Database Design; CMPS 367 Advanced Topics; CMPS 369 Web Application Development; CMPS 370 Cyber and Network Defense; CMPS 373 Object Oriented Programming; CMPS 375 Mobile Robotics; DATA 301 Data Analysis & Visualization. [1]

Career Pathways courses: PATH 001 Career Pathways Mod 1, PATH 002 Career Pathways Mod 2, and PATH 003 Career Pathways Mod 3. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-CMPS)

Adherence to this policy, procedure, and the confidential Cybersecurity Protocols & Compliance Manual seeks to ensure not only the protection of the College’s digital assets but also the continued growth and success of the College. question: is there an MBA at ramapo? and is it part time

body.answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers a Master of Business Administration (MBA) through the Anisfield School of Business. [2][3] The published MBA overview describes a 42-credit, 20-month cohort program with a fall start only; it does not say whether students can attend part time. [2]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [24]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: if I fail a class can I retake it and does the old grade get replaced in my gpa

body.answer:
Yes. Undergraduate and graduate students may retake a failed course as many times as needed to achieve a passing grade; register for it as normal. [14][18]

Retaking alone does not replace the old grade: all grades count in your cumulative GPA. To exclude one previous grade from your cumulative GPA, after retaking the course, request grade replacement using the [Grade Replacement Request Form](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/forms-transcripts/repeat-course-form/). [14][17] The prior grade remains on your transcript with an “R” before it. [17]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [30]

Sources: [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#retaking-courses) [17](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#grade-replacement1) [18](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#retaking-courses) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what's the deadline to withdraw from a course and what shows up on my transcript if i do

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [31]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

If you’re in a Session II course, the deadline is Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The deadlines for Session I and full-semester courses have passed. [31]

After the refund period ends, you may withdraw by the deadline; there is no refund, and a “W” will be recorded on your transcript. [12] You can withdraw through Web Self Service; students with registration holds can use the Withdrawal Form or email the Registrar from their Ramapo email account with their name, Ramapo ID (R#), CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title. You may not withdraw after the published deadline. [12]

Simply stopping attendance or notifying your instructor is not an official withdrawal; without officially withdrawing through the Registrar’s Office, you remain registered and may receive an “F” or “FN.” [4]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [32]

Sources: [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#grading-system) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how many credits do I need for a business minor and what courses count

body.answer:
The catalog lists these business minors: Business Analytics Minor and International Business Minor [3]. It publishes no total credit count for either minor [1][2]. The catalog’s general minor rule says a minor must include between 16 and 24 credits (including all non-general education prerequisites and excluding all lab science course credits) [7].

**Business Analytics and Applied AI Minor — Minor** (also published: International Business BA) [1]
Required courses, all of: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS; INFO 224 PRINCIPLES OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY; INFO 310 BUSINESS ANALYTICS I; INFO 345 AI FOR BUSINESS: HARNESSING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE. Electives: select 2 courses from ECON 310 ECONOMETRICS; INFO 233 INTRODUCTION TO PROGRAMMING; INFO 311 BUSINESS ANALYTICS II; INFO 320 TOOLS FOR ANALYTICS AND AI; INFO 332 DATABASE MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS; INFO 333 DATA VISUALIZATION; INFO 422 DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEMS; MGMT 373 MANAGEMENT SCIENCE; MKTG 330 MARKETING RESEARCH [1].

**International Business Minor** (also published: International Business BA) [2]
Prerequisites, all of: ECON 102 INTRODUCTION TO MACROECONOMICS; IBUS 326 FUNDAMENTALS OF INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS. Select 1 International Foundation Course: ECON 323 COMPARATIVE ECONOMIC SYSTEMS; ECON 325 INTERNATIONAL ECONOMICS; FINC 415 MULTINATIONAL FINANCE; IBUS 305 POLITICS OF INTERNATIONAL INVESTMENT; IBUS 330 FUNDAMENTALS OF IMPORTING AND EXPORTING; MKTG 350 INTERNATIONAL MARKETING. Select 1 Geopolitical Course: BADM 316 WORLD POLITICAL ECONOMY; IBUS 305 POLITICS OF INTERNATIONAL INVESTMENT; IBUS 315 INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS IMMERSION COURSE IN JAPAN & KOREA; IBUS 321 CHINA AND OTHER BUSINESS ENVIRONMENTS IN ASIA; IBUS 322 INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS IMMERSION COURSE IN CHINA; IBUS 335 DOING BUSINESS IN LATIN AMERICA; IBUS 336 DOING BUSINESS IN AFRICA; IBUS 337 IMMERSION COURSE IN PERU; IBUS 340 EUROPEAN BUSINESS COMMUNITY; POLI 205 COMPARATIVE POLITICS. Select 1 Additional Elective Course: BADM 316 WORLD POLITICAL ECONOMY; ECON 323 COMPARATIVE ECONOMIC SYSTEMS; FINC 415 MULTINATIONAL FINANCE; IBUS 300 INDEPENDENT STUDY: INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS; IBUS 315 INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS IMMERSION COURSE IN JAPAN & KOREA; IBUS 321 CHINA AND OTHER BUSINESS ENVIRONMENTS IN ASIA; IBUS 322 INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS IMMERSION COURSE IN CHINA; IBUS 330 FUNDAMENTALS OF IMPORTING AND EXPORTING; IBUS 335 DOING BUSINESS IN LATIN AMERICA; IBUS 336 DOING BUSINESS IN AFRICA; IBUS 340 EUROPEAN BUSINESS COMMUNITY; MKTG 350 INTERNATIONAL MARKETING; POLI 205 COMPARATIVE POLITICS [2].

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [27]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MN-BAAI) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MN-IBUS) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what GPA do I need to make the dean's list and what happens if im on academic probation

body.answer:
To qualify for the Dean’s List, you must be a matriculated undergraduate student, complete a minimum of 12 cumulative credits (not including “P” grades), have no incomplete grades for that semester, attain a semester GPA of at least 3.5 and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0. Part-time students taking fewer than 12 credits per semester are not eligible. The list is published at the end of fall and spring semesters. [14]

For undergraduate academic probation: You are placed on probation after a cumulative GPA below 2.0 for two consecutive semesters, and cannot appeal your standing. Toward the middle of the Fall and Spring semester, the Provost or designee emails students on probation with a reminder of their standing and actions to take once grades are posted at the end of the semester. If you achieve a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0, you return to good standing after probation. If your cumulative GPA remains below 2.0 but you achieve a semester GPA of at least 2.5, you are placed on Continued Probation for one semester. If you were on Continued Probation, achieving a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0 returns you to good standing after probation. [9]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [26]

Sources: [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#undergraduate-academic-standing) [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dean-s-list) [26](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
To qualify for the Dean’s List, you must be a matriculated undergraduate student, complete a minimum of 12 cumulative credits (not including “P” grades), have no incomplete grades for that semester, attain a semester GPA of at least 3.5 and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0. Part-time students taking fewer than 12 credits per semester are not eligible. The list is published at the end of fall and spring semesters. [14]

For undergraduate academic probation: You are placed on probation after a cumulative GPA below 2.0 for two consecutive semesters, and cannot appeal your standing. Toward the middle of the Fall and Spring semester, the Provost or designee emails students on probation with a reminder of their standing and actions to take once grades are posted at the end of the semester. If you achieve a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0, you return to good standing after probation. If your cumulative GPA remains below 2.0 but you achieve a semester GPA of at least 2.5, you are placed on Continued Probation for one semester. If you were on Continued Probation, achieving a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0 returns you to good standing after probation. [9]

question: what are the general education requirements for incoming first year students? like how many courses in each category

body.answer:
Ramapo students take ten General Education courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two out of three distribution categories. [9]

Take all four keystone courses: First Year Seminar; Social Science Inquiry; Critical Reading & Writing 102; and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. [9]

Take one course from each keystone category: Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Critical Reading & Writing 102 and Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits. [9]

Take one course in two of these three distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics. [9] At least one course must be offered by a school other than the one that houses your major. [9]

First Year Seminar must be taken during the fall semester of your first year. [15]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [28]

Sources: [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
Ramapo students take ten General Education courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two out of three distribution categories. [9]

Take all four keystone courses: First Year Seminar; Social Science Inquiry; Critical Reading & Writing 102; and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. [9]

Take one course from each keystone category: Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Critical Reading & Writing 102 and Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits. [9]

Take one course in two of these three distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics. [9] At least one course must be offered by a school other than the one that houses your major. [9]

First Year Seminar must be taken during the fall semester of your first year. [15]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [28]

question: how do i get a parking permit as a commuter

body.answer:
Apply online through the [Parking Permit Registration](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/opr/OPRMain.aspx?IsAuth=1&groupid=102&groupname=PUBLIC+SAFETY) link. Commuter students may register two vehicles on one permit at no additional fee, but each vehicle must be registered, and only one may be parked on campus at a time. [1][7]

Ensure the parking fee has been applied to your student account. [7] After applying, returning commuter students can pick up their permit at the Public Safety ID Office Monday through Friday during normal operating hours. For pickup after 3 pm at the Public Safety Office Main Desk, email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request a different pickup time. [7][10]

The parking fee automatically appears on your term bill; off-campus students are charged a seven percent (7%) sales tax. [10] Contact Public Safety for questions. [10]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [31]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [31]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [31]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I lost my student ID card, where do I get a replacement and does it cost anything?

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Contact the ID room at publicsafety@ramapo.edu. They will reprint your card and leave it at the front of the Public Safety Office for pickup; you’ll receive an email when it’s ready. The replacement fee for a lost ID is $25. [1]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [33]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [33]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/id-cards/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: which is easier, biology or psychology major? I have a 2.8 gpa right now, do you think I can still get into the nursing program

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

The college does not say which major is easier. Its published descriptions show different requirements: Biology has biology, chemistry, physics, math, and elective requirements; Psychology includes required psychology courses and choices across eight categories. [1][2] The Center for Student Success says to choose based on what you love to study and where your natural skills point you. [8]

The Center for Student Success helps students choose a major. It recommends focusing on top choices, choosing classes that help you decide, and talking with faculty in those majors. [10][11]

A 2.8 GPA alone does not establish whether you can get into nursing; the requirements depend on the track and applicant type. For the generic BSN, the published page lists pre-nursing courses: one of MATH 108 or PSYC 242, plus BIOL 212 and lab, BIOL 214 and lab, BIOL 216 and lab, CHEM 111 and lab, and PSYC 101. Students must earn C+ or better in all nursing courses. [4] The accelerated BSN is for prospective students with a non-Nursing bachelor’s degree or at least 60 credits from a regionally-accredited institution; Bridge courses require C+ or better to proceed to nursing courses, and Nursing courses require C+ or better. [3] Transfer applicants to accelerated BSN need a 3.0 cumulative GPA or above. [5] First-year applicants applying to Nursing through EOF need a 3.0 or higher, four years of math and science, and strong grades in math and science. [6] Ramapo's nursing major requires a 2.3 GPA for degree eligibility. [15]

I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

The college does not say which major is easier. Its published descriptions show different requirements: Biology has biology, chemistry, physics, math, and elective requirements; Psychology includes required psychology courses and choices across eight categories. [1][2] The Center for Student Success says to choose based on what you love to study and where your natural skills point you. [8]

The Center for Student Success helps students choose a major. It recommends focusing on top choices, choosing classes that help you decide, and talking with faculty in those majors. [10][11]

A 2.8 GPA alone does not establish whether you can get into nursing; the requirements depend on the track and applicant type. For the generic BSN, the published page lists pre-nursing courses: one of MATH 108 or PSYC 242, plus BIOL 212 and lab, BIOL 214 and lab, BIOL 216 and lab, CHEM 111 and lab, and PSYC 101. Students must earn C+ or better in all nursing courses. [4] The accelerated BSN is for prospective students with a non-Nursing bachelor’s degree or at least 60 credits from a regionally-accredited institution; Bridge courses require C+ or better to proceed to nursing courses, and Nursing courses require C+ or better. [3] Transfer applicants to accelerated BSN need a 3.0 cumulative GPA or above. [5] First-year applicants applying to Nursing through EOF need a 3.0 or higher, four years of math and science, and strong grades in math and science. [6] Ramapo's nursing major requires a 2.3 GPA for degree eligibility. [15]

question: i have a hold on my account and cant register for spring classes. how do i find out what its for and who do i contact to get it removed

body.answer:
In RCNJ Experience, click the Registration box, then Open Registration Dashboard, then Register for Classes and choose Spring to view registration information. [20]

For an outstanding balance, Student Accounts says a Hold Flag prevents registration and is removed once the account is paid in full. You may still have a hold from another office or department. [1] If you are unsure what the hold is for, contact the office responsible for it. For an academic or financial admissions hold, contact the Center for Student Success or Student Accounts, respectively. [22]

Student Accounts and the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) can help identify the appropriate next steps.

- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [31]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [31]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/payment-policies/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/registration-faq/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/returning-student/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do I request an official transcript to send to another school? I'm a transfer student and need it for a grad program application

body.answer:
Request an electronic official transcript through the National Student Clearinghouse: [https://tsorder.studentclearinghouse.org/school/select](https://tsorder.studentclearinghouse.org/school/select). The fee is $4.90 per request (nonrefundable). Orders are typically processed within 1–3 business days, and the Clearinghouse will notify you at each step. The email link is available for 30 days. Clear any holds before ordering. You cannot change the recipient’s email after placing the order or cancel it; to correct an email address, place a new order. [2]

For a paper transcript, complete the Official Transcript Request Form: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Official-Transcript-Request-Form-FILLABLE.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Official-Transcript-Request-Form-FILLABLE.pdf). Paper copies are free and typically processed in 3–5 business days; peak periods may take longer. Paper transcripts can be mailed to another institution, but cannot be emailed or faxed. [2]

For your graduate application, official transcripts must be sent directly from previous colleges. Ramapo Graduate Admissions accepts electronic transcripts at graduate@ramapo.edu or mail at: Ramapo College of New Jersey, Attn: Admissions, 505 Ramapo Valley Road, Mahwah, NJ 07430. [15]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [34]
- **Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [34]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/forms-transcripts/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I live on campus and my roommate situation is really bad. what's the process to request a room change?

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Visit the [Room Change Process webpage](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/), review the step-by-step instructions, and submit the digital Room Change Request Form during the open period. Check the [Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/critical-housing-dates-deadlines-calendar/) to understand how a room change might affect you. [1]

For Spring 2027, submit the form no later than 12:00 pm Tuesday, November 24, 2026. Outcome responses will be sent via email by 4:30 pm Friday, December 4, 2026. Approved students move to their new assignments on Spring 2027 Check-in Day, January 18, 2027. You must completely vacate your current assignment at the end of Fall semester when you check out. Dates are subject to change. [3]

Requests are not guaranteed and are not first-come, first-served; placement depends on suitable available space and other factors. Complete the form carefully. [1][4] Once approved, you must check in to the new assignment; otherwise a $75 improper checkout fee will be charged. Approved changes cannot be canceled. Review the room-change page for other considerations, including housing and meal plan costs. [4]

If the open period has ended, contact Housing & Residence Life for guidance on available options. [3]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [30]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [31]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can i switch my meal plan mid semester or is that locked in

body.answer:
Yes—you can change your meal plan. For Spring 2027, requests are accepted through January 25, 2027 [3]. Email mealplan@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email account with your complete first and last name, Banner ID Number (R-Number), and meal plan choice [3]. Housing & Residence Life says changes may be made up until the 100% refund date [1]; Student Accounts lists that date as January 25, 2027 (minus meal usage), with no 50% refund period [12].

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [35]

answer:
Yes—you can change your meal plan. For Spring 2027, requests are accepted through January 25, 2027 [3]. Email mealplan@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email account with your complete first and last name, Banner ID Number (R-Number), and meal plan choice [3]. Housing & Residence Life says changes may be made up until the 100% refund date [1]; Student Accounts lists that date as January 25, 2027 (minus meal usage), with no 50% refund period [12].

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [35]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [35]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deadlines/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I have ADHD and want extra time on exams. How do I register for disability accommodations and who handles that?

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

The Office of Specialized Services (OSS) handles student disability accommodations. To register, initiate contact with OSS to request services and submit comprehensive documentation of your disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist. See “How To Request OSS Services” for more information. [9]

Once registered, accommodations are determined based on your documented needs. Extended testing time is a potential accommodation, not automatic; accommodations are case-by-case. [14][17]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [34]

Sources: [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/what-faculty-need-to-know-about-students-with-disabilities/) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/disabilities-and-teaching-strategies-accommodations/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i make an appointment at counseling services? is it free for students

body.answer:
For regular therapy, call to schedule an initial, in-person triage appointment. It lasts 60 minutes; staff will contact you the Monday after your appointment to discuss next steps. [1] You can also stop by the Counseling Center in room D-216. [2]

Counseling Services offers free and confidential services, including short-term individual counseling. [6] The Counseling Center can help with appointment scheduling.

**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [29]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/faq/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: someone broke into my car in lot H last night. how do I report it to public safety, is there a number to call

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Call Public Safety at (201) 684-6666 (or extension 6666 on an internal Ramapo College phone), or go to its office on the ground floor of C-wing, Room C-102. Public Safety is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. [3][4]

Describe what happened, who was involved, where and when it happened, and how or why, if you know. Be as specific as possible; give your name and the names of any witnesses. Report theft and vehicle damage as soon as discovered. [1][3]

You can also submit the [Report An Incident form](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/report-an-incident-form). Submissions are read and responded to during business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.; after-hours, weekend, and holiday submissions are addressed the next business day. [6][7]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [31]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [31]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-report/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/report-an-incident-form/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-report/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: where can i print stuff on campus and how many pages do i get

body.answer:
Active students can print from a mobile device or laptop to swipe-to-release printers in the Learning Commons and Fishbowl. [3] The Library has printers on the first floor across from the computer lab/classroom, in the 2nd Floor Print Room (205), in the 3rd Floor Print Room (311), and on the fourth floor in Room 408 and the help desk area. Wireless printing is also available; see the [instructions](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/wp-content/uploads/sites/301/2024/01/mobileprintdoc.pdf). [4]

- **Library**: Phone: (201) 684-7575. Email: circ@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons. [33]

question: my ramapo email password expired and i cant get on the wifi. who do i call for help

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Call the IT Help Desk at 201-684-7777. It is the first point of contact for IT service requests. [1] You can also email helpdesk@ramapo.edu. [2]

For the password reset, visit [https://password.ramapo.edu/](https://password.ramapo.edu/). If you don’t know your password, use “Activate Email.” [5] Before changing it, forget the saved Wi-Fi network on your devices; afterward, reconnect using your new password. [5]

**IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [33]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/help-desk/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/help-desk/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/important-notes-for-password-reset/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: What's my current account balance and when is my payment due?

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

I don’t have verified information about your individual current account balance. To check your account, log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), locate the Student Account Info card, and click Bill & Payment Suite. [12] Your eBill is a statement of your account at a given point in time; activity or charges since it was generated can change the amount owed. From the eBill page, click “activity since your last statement” to see activity since your last bill. [9]

The Spring 2027 payment deadline is December 16, 2026. Students registering or adjusting their schedules after that date must pay on the day they register or adjust their schedule. Missing the deadline may result in a $200 late payment fee for each missed payment deadline, deregistration, and dehousing. [2][3] For help, contact Student Accounts.

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [26]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deadlines/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [26](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: which dorm is better for sophomores, and should I take the 19 meal swipe plan or the 14?

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

The pages provided don’t say which dorm is better for sophomores, and they don’t describe 19- or 14-meal swipe plans, so I can’t recommend a dorm or plan from verified information. The published information identifies Pine and Mackin as first-year halls [12][13], and says residents in traditional residence halls must have a meal plan [2]. For details about available meal plans and help deciding, contact Housing & Residence Life. You can change a Spring 2027 meal plan through January 25, 2027. Email mealplan@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email account with your complete first and last name, Banner ID Number (R-Number), and meal plan choice. Requests take at least three business days to process; you’ll receive a confirmation email when completed. Don’t send multiple requests [2][10].

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [22]

For details about available meal plans and help deciding, contact Housing & Residence Life. You can change a Spring 2027 meal plan through January 25, 2027.
